subproblem.title: Integer lattice approximation with bounded boundary masses in every dimension
subproblem.statement: Assume DeformationTheorem (Simon 5.3, frozen statement). Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let X ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞. Then there are ρ_k > 0, β_k : LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P → ℤ and P_k ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with IsLatticeChain ρ_k β_k P_k for all k, P_k ⇀ X weakly, and sup_k M(∂P_k) < ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: DeformationTheorem → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity X → X.mass < ∞ → X.boundary.mass < ∞ → ∃ (ρ : ℕ → ℝ) (β : ℕ → LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) P → ℤ) (Pk : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)), (∀ k, 0 < ρ k) ∧ (∀ k, IsLatticeChain (ρ k) (fun F => (β k F : ℝ)) (Pk k)) ∧ WeaklyConvergesOn Pk X ∧ (⨆ k, (Pk k).boundary.mass) < ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (P7) of the parent proof (polyhedral approximation with mass bounds; first case via `DeformationTheorem`, second case via the printed steps (27)–(37), here the sibling top_dim_lattice_approx) and the first half of step 4 (the printed proof of 6.2, first paragraph: “Evidently (1), (2) give P_k(ω) → T(ω)”), with the trivial dimensions of step 1. `DeformationTheorem` is a hypothesis of this statement; it is discharged by the sibling node root.deformation-a1 in the parent's assembly.

Notation. |α| = `covectorEuclideanNorm α`; ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)| (finite for test forms: continuous with compact support); M = `mass`.

0. (Mass estimate.) If Y ∈ D_k(ℝ^P) has M(Y) < ∞ then |Y(ω)| ≤ M(Y)‖ω‖ for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^P). Proof: for every s > ‖ω‖ (s > 0) the forms ±ω/s satisfy |±ω(x)/s| = |ω(x)|/s ≤ 1 (|·| is absolutely homogeneous), so they are mass-admissible and ±Y(ω)/s ≤ M(Y); let s ↓ ‖ω‖.
1. (Case P < m + 1.) Any m+1 vectors of ℝ^P are linearly dependent, so every (m+1)-covector vanishes, every test form in D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) is 0, and X(ω) = X(0) = 0 for all ω. Take ρ_k := 1, β_k := 0, Pk := 0: `IsLatticeChain 1 0 0` holds (both sides are 0; the index type is even empty), Pk(ω) = 0 = X(ω) so Pk ⇀ X, and M(∂0) = M(0) = 0.
2. (Case P = m + 1.) This is exactly the sibling top_dim_lattice_approx (with `Eucl P` = `Eucl (m+1)` and `LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P` = `LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) (m+1)` after substituting P = m + 1).
3. (Case P ≥ m + 2.) Write P = m + 1 + ℓ with ℓ ≥ 1 (so `Eucl P` is `Eucl (m+1+ℓ)` after substitution). Let C = C(m,ℓ) be the constant of `DeformationTheorem` for (m, ℓ). For k ∈ ℕ put ρ_k := 1/(k+1) > 0 and apply `DeformationTheorem` to X (M(X) + M(∂X) < ∞) and ρ_k: there are Pc_k ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P), β′_k : `LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P` → ℝ, R_k ∈ D_{m+2}(ℝ^P), S_k ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with `IsLatticeChain ρ_k β′_k Pc_k`, X(ω) − Pc_k(ω) = R_k(dω) + S_k(ω) for all ω (R_k.boundary ω = R_k(dω)), M(∂Pc_k) ≤ C M(∂X), M(R_k) ≤ Cρ_kM(X), M(S_k) ≤ Cρ_kM(∂X), and, X being integer multiplicity, every β′_k(F) is an integer; choose β_k(F) ∈ ℤ with β′_k(F) = β_k(F), so `IsLatticeChain ρ_k (fun F => (β_k F : ℝ)) Pc_k`. Put Pk := Pc_k.
 (a) Weak convergence. Fix ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P). M(R_k), M(S_k) < ∞, so by step 0: |X(ω) − Pk(ω)| ≤ |R_k(dω)| + |S_k(ω)| ≤ M(R_k)‖dω‖ + M(S_k)‖ω‖ ≤ Cρ_k(M(X)‖dω‖ + M(∂X)‖ω‖) → 0 as k → ∞ (M(X), M(∂X), ‖dω‖, ‖ω‖ are finite and ρ_k → 0). Hence Pk ⇀ X.
 (b) Boundary masses. M(∂Pk) ≤ C M(∂X) for all k, so sup_k M(∂Pk) ≤ C M(∂X) < ∞.
4. In all cases we have ρ_k > 0, integer β_k, `IsLatticeChain ρ_k β_k Pk`, Pk ⇀ X and sup_k M(∂Pk) < ∞.
proof_key_steps: For P < m+1 all (m+1)-forms vanish, X = 0, and the zero chain works.
For P = m+1 use the sibling top_dim_lattice_approx.
For P = m+1+ℓ, ℓ ≥ 1, apply DeformationTheorem at scale ρ_k = 1/(k+1): X − P_k = ∂R_k + S_k with integer coefficients, M(∂P_k) ≤ CM(∂X), M(R_k) ≤ Cρ_kM(X), M(S_k) ≤ Cρ_kM(∂X).
|X(ω) − P_k(ω)| ≤ M(R_k)‖dω‖ + M(S_k)‖ω‖ → 0, so P_k ⇀ X, and sup_k M(∂P_k) ≤ CM(∂X) < ∞.

audit.reason: The dimension split is exhaustive. The declared top-dimensional child handles equality of dimensions; the explicit DeformationTheorem hypothesis supplies integer coefficients and the required mass estimates in positive codimension. The zero-current case and weak-convergence estimate complete the exact contract.
